title: Share of US firms using AI (firm-weighted)
source_name: Census Business Trends and Outlook Survey (BTOS), national

breaks.note: Question changed from AI use 'in producing goods or services' to 'in any business function'

annotations.label: Census question wording changed: term and examples changed, 'AI' relabelled 'Super Intelligence or SI (formerly AI)', and new examples given (from the collection starting 19 October 2026)

notes: National, all-sector, firm-weighted share answering Yes (the core AI-use question), with Census standard errors (column se, percentage points). Each estimate is dated by the end of its two-week collection period (Census sample date in parentheses). The question actually asked in each period. Before 17 November 2025 (periods 202319 to 202520, AI Core Questions.xlsx): In the last two weeks, did this business use Artificial Intelligence (AI) in producing goods or services? (Examples of AI: machine learning, natural language processing, virtual agents, voice recognition, etc.) From 17 November 2025 to 18 October 2026: In the last two weeks, did this business use Artificial Intelligence (AI) in any of its business functions? (Examples of AI: machine learning, natural language processing, virtual agents, voice recognition, etc.) From 19 October 2026: Between MMM DD - MMM DD, did this business use Super Intelligence or SI (formerly referred to as Artificial Intelligence or AI) in any of its business functions? (Examples of SI use include: SI-powered data analysis; generative SI for marketing, product design, or coding; virtual SI agents for customer service; SI-powered forecasting or pricing; SI-driven computer vision for quality control, etc.) National.xlsx prints the October 2026 wording for all of its periods (202524 to 202623), including those before 19 October 2026: In the last two weeks, did this business use Super Intelligence or SI (formerly referred to as Artificial Intelligence or AI) in any of its business functions? (Examples of SI use include: SI-powered data analysis; generative SI for marketing, product design, or coding; virtual SI agents for customer service; SI-powered forecasting or pricing; SI-driven computer vision for quality control, etc.) Census published no estimate for sample dates 202521 to 202523 (collections 2025-10-06 to 2025-11-16), so the series has a gap before the wording change. The pre-17-November-2025 and later wordings are not directly comparable; the break date is the first collection of the new wording. Sources: Census's wording notice of 3 December 2025 and the BTOS instruments. The October 2026 change of both the term and the examples is shown as a chart marker, not a break.
